$comment: Single source of truth for what lives in this monorepo and what CI may run.
* Every top-level project directory MUST have exactly one entry here.
* A check is only ever set to `true` after it has been observed passing.
Flipping a flag optimistically is how a repository ends up with red
* Every `false` carries a `notes` string explaining the blocker.

projects.notes: No lint or test script defined.
Vue 3 SPA, plain JavaScript. lint migrated from .eslintrc.cjs to flat config for ESLint 10 and observed clean; the check-only form is lint, the mutating one is lint:fix. No test script.

Clean-architecture implementation with 42 unit tests. install, lint, build and test each observed passing from a clean checkout before these flags were set. ESLint runs on flat config; Cypress is not wired into CI and its binary download is skipped.

Nuxt 4 with six numbered layers, each a step in the same refactor. Declares pnpm@9.15.5 and commits pnpm-lock.yaml, and CI honours both: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` verifies the lockfile as well as installing from it. All four checks pass: 363 lint errors and a test suite that could not start were both traced to dependencies the project used but never declared - typescript, without which @nuxt/eslint-config silently treats it as a JavaScript project, and a vitest 3 stack that cannot drive nuxt 4's vite 8. 104 tests pass, 4 skipped by the author.

Angular 22 + Material. typescript majors are held: @angular/compiler-cli peers `>=6.0 <6.1` and the build dies inside readConfiguration on 7 (issue #1289). test runs the Karma/Jasmine suite headless - the script passes --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadless, since bare `ng test` watches and wants a real browser. jasmine is held at 5.x: 6 made its env methods non-writable and zone.js patches them by assignment, which kills the suite at load (issue #1407). 12 tests, verified headless. No lint script.

@astrojs/check@0.9.10 peers typescript@^5||^6 while this project runs ^7.0.2, so npm ci needs --legacy-peer-deps (recorded in installFlags). Same family as the typescript hold: the tool has not widened for TS 7 yet. Tracked in issue #1289. No lint or test script is defined, so both stay off.

SvelteKit with Lucia-style sessions and Google OAuth via arctic. $env/static/private inlines secrets at build time, so the build needs every name in .env.example present - the values in env are placeholders, not credentials, and the artefact is discarded. The same names are what `svelte-kit sync` reads to generate the $env/static/public declarations, so typecheck needs them too. test stays off: `npm test` chains test:e2e, which wants Playwright browsers and a seeded database, and it shells out to pnpm, which this project does not install with. There is also a test:unit script - plain `vitest`, no pnpm, no browser, no database - and it does run and pass. It is not worth enabling: tests/unit holds one file whose single assertion is expect(1 + 2).toBe(3), the scaffolding demo. Gating CI on it would buy a green tick that tests nothing about this project. The check earns its place when tests/unit has a test of the codebase. That also leaves vite-node uncovered: it appears only in db:seed and db:clear, so a vite-node bump has to be exercised by hand against a scratch libsql file.

prebuild runs prisma generate, which needs no database. Prisma is on 7 with the pg driver adapter (ADR 0004); schema push and a live query were verified against a local Postgres 16. lint stays off and is blocked upstream: eslint-config-next 16.3.3 bundles typescript-eslint 8.68, which refuses TypeScript 7 outright - "typescript-eslint does not support TS 7.0" - and this project is on typescript 7.0.2, so the run dies inside eslint-config-next before any rule executes. Same blocker as rn_clean_architecture, tracked at typescript-eslint#10940 and issue #1430. The config itself is migrated and correct, so the check flips the day that resolves. No test script is defined.

React Native 0.87 + inversify. Babel majors and jest 30 are held: @react-native/babel-preset asserts ^7.0.0-0 on @babel/core internally, invisible to the resolver (issue #1296). jasmine has no part here. lint is blocked upstream, on one thing only: typescript-eslint 8.68 refuses TypeScript 7 outright - "typescript-eslint does not support TS 7.0" - and this project is on typescript 7.0.2, so eslint dies loading eslint-plugin-jest before any rule runs. Tracked at typescript-eslint#10940 and issue #1430; the check flips the day it lands, with no change needed here. Three earlier faults were ours and are fixed: eslint.config.mjs imported @eslint/eslintrc without declaring it (eslint 9 supplied it transitively, eslint 10 does not), which killed the run with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND before any config loaded; FlatCompat resolved plugins from the project root rather than from the config package that declares them, so eslint-plugin-react was reported missing - resolvePluginsRelativeTo fixes it, pointed at the dirname of the package entry point because its exports map hides ./package.json; and installing @eslint/eslintrc needs the --legacy-peer-deps already in installFlags, since @react-native/eslint-config 0.87 peers eslint ^8 || ^9 against this project's eslint 10. build is off because no build script is defined - React Native builds through Xcode and Gradle, not npm. test runs jest: 6 tests, verified. It needed constructor injection first - Babel rejects a decorated field with a definite-assignment assertion - plus babel-plugin-transform-typescript-metadata, since Babel does not implement TypeScript parameter decorators on its own. typecheck runs `tsc --noEmit`, clean. It could not run at all until tsconfig.json started extending @react-native/typescript-config instead of restating a drifted copy of it - the copy kept moduleResolution=node10 and baseUrl, both removed in TypeScript 7, and lost skipLibCheck and types:[jest] (issue #1360).
Frontend of the Flask app. The Python API alongside it is covered separately as solid-flask-web-app/api (install, ruff and 75 tests). No lint or test script is defined.

The Engineering Atlas. Nuxt 4 + Nuxt Content. better-sqlite3 13 sits outside @nuxt/content's peerOptional ^12.5.0, so npm ci needs --legacy-peer-deps (recorded in installFlags). That combination was verified by running the built server, not just by building it - see docs/DEPENDENCIES.md. Tracked in issue #1289. No lint or test script is defined.

build runs tsc. A `typecheck` script is also available. No lint script is defined. test is npm's placeholder, `echo "Error: no test specified" && exit 1`, so it can only fail. typecheck stays off too, but for a different reason: it is `tsc --noEmit` over the same files build already compiles with `tsc`, so it would double the job for no extra signal (issue #1360).

NestJS SOLID demonstrations. Prisma 7 with the better-sqlite3 driver adapter (ADR 0004); prebuild runs prisma generate, which needs no database. typescript held at ^6 (issue #1296). lint migrated to ESLint 10 flat config and observed clean. Nest 12 ships pure ESM - every package is "type": "module" with no require condition in its exports - so jest cannot load @nestjs/testing through its CommonJS transform and dies at import with SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export'. test therefore runs under NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-vm-modules with ts-jest in ESM mode (module esnext, moduleResolution bundler, overridden per transform so the CommonJS build is untouched): 1 suite, 1 test, observed running rather than merely resolving. The build still emits CommonJS, and node dist/main starts only because Node 22.12+ can require() an ESM graph, so the node 22 pin above is load-bearing - the same dist on Node 20 would not boot, even though @nestjs/core still declares engines >= 20. test:e2e is not a CI check but now runs (1 test, boots the app against dev.db): it needed the src/* path alias mapped, which no jest-e2e config had ever configured, and a default supertest import in place of import * as, which is not callable under ESM.

Express 5 + TypeORM + tsyringe. typescript held at ^6: ts-node needs the programmatic compiler API removed in TS 7, so the dev server and jest both die on import (issue #1296). lint runs eslint 10 against a flat config. build is `tsc` to dist/. test is a real suite: 6 unit specs against in-memory repositories plus one integration spec that runs the migrations and reads back through CategoryRepository, so CI starts the runner's PostgreSQL and creates the database named in the postgres field. The DataSource reads DATABASE_URL when set, which is what that step exports. 21 tests, verified against a live PostgreSQL 16 from an empty database.

Bun + Hono + Postgres. Registered under the bun ecosystem so Dependabot writes bun.lock. lint is biome, check-only (22 files, 2 infos, exit 0); the mutating form lives in lint:fix so CI checks rather than rewrites. test is a real integration suite: it shells out to drizzle db:push and truncates the table between cases, so CI starts the runner's PostgreSQL and creates the database named in the postgres field. That step also exports DATABASE_URL, because a postgresql://user:pass@host string in this env block makes the runner drop the whole matrix as a suspected secret. 4 tests, 8 assertions, verified against a live Postgres 16. .env.test is gitignored and unnecessary - the suite passes with the file absent. No build script is defined; bun runs the TypeScript directly.
Single-file operational script; no build step. No lint script is defined, and test is npm's placeholder, `echo "Error: no test specified" && exit 1`, so it can only fail.

Umbrella entry. The three Poetry projects beneath it — backend, frontend and pipelines — carry their own manifest entries and CI checks. Nothing runs at this level: install, build, lint and test are all off because there is no project here to run them against.
Streamlit UI. install runs `poetry check --lock` then `poetry install`; 6 tests pass. No build step and no linter configured. No linter is configured, so lint stays off.

Ingestion pipeline. install verified (~3.5 min; the torch/transformers tree is ~5.7 GB). test is 9 tests, all passing, and needs neither a live Milvus nor network access - verified by running the suite with HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 and the proxy variables unset. The recorded reason it used to be off was wrong: test_milvus_connector_collection_creation does not need a Milvus server, it was simply missing the mock_models fixture its two sibling tests apply, so constructing a MilvusConnector reached Hugging Face to download all-MiniLM-L6-v2. test_markdown_processor was failing on a real defect - parse_markdown loaded the front matter and then discarded it, returning a header dict built by indexing an HTML string as if it were a mapping, so metadata was always empty. build is off because a Poetry library has no build step. lint is ruff, run as `poetry run ruff check .` and observed clean: it found 8 real problems - six unused imports, a dead local in process_markdown and a bare `except` in main's shutdown path that would have swallowed KeyboardInterrupt - and all eight are fixed. black, isort, mypy and pylint stay in the dev group but gate nothing: black alone wanted a 754-line reformat that would have found none of those eight.

FastAPI service. install verified (~3 min). test is 5 import-and-construct checks: every module imports, app.app is a FastAPI carrying the documented routes, and tools stays lazy. They exist because install was the only check and PR #1416 shipped a langgraph/langgraph-prebuilt pairing that installs cleanly and cannot import - CI was green over a backend that could not start (issue #1423). Those two are pinned in pyproject with the reason inline. build is off because a Poetry service has no build step. lint is ruff, run as `poetry run ruff check .` and observed clean. It selects more than ruff's default: the default (E4, E7, E9, F) found nothing here, so gating on it would have been a green that could not go red. I (imports), UP (pyupgrade, safe outright at python ^3.12) and B (bugbear) are added, and B is what earned it - three handlers raised HTTPException inside an except block with no `from e`, losing the exception chain on every 500 and 503 this service returns. test_notebook.ipynb is excluded as interactive scratch. black, mypy and pylint stay in the dev group but gate nothing.

Flask API. Its own manifest entry is solid-flask-web-app/api; the frontend is covered separately as solid-flask-web-app/ui. Umbrella entry. The two projects beneath it - api and ui - carry their own manifest entries and CI checks, so install, build, lint and test are all off here.

Flask API, pip + setuptools rather than Poetry. Python 3.13 to match Dockerfile.api. mysqlclient builds from source, so it needs MySQL client headers — declared in systemPackages. install, ruff and 75 tests all observed passing before these flags were set. No build step; the service runs from source.

Six Spring/Java modules behind an aggregator pom.xml. build runs `mvn -B -DskipTests package`, test runs `mvn -B verify` (4 tests, all in patient-service). billing/clinical/scheduling are domain-only modules — entity, repository port and use case, Lombok and the JDK only — so their POMs are plain Java libraries rather than Spring Boot applications. install is off because `mvn verify` resolves dependencies itself, so a separate install step would only download the same tree twice. lint is off because the pom configures no checkstyle, spotless or pmd plugin.
